A.trend: Traced monthly points, quantified early-to-late decline, peak and censoring; chart omits the critical-series decomposition available in the response.
A.comparison: The 13.69-to-0.58 ratio recomputes to 23.6x, defines the corpus baseline, and notes that it is not an election-only comparison.
A.chart: The monthly chart traces all points and supports the trend claim, but does not chart the supported tone or geography facets.
A.drilldown: It names breakdown fields but supplies no executable follow-up calls that returned data.
A.export: Monthly CSV has traced values and provenance JSON with call, window, unit and coverage; it is referenced in prose.
A.repro: The primary call, args and window are listed; reported figures and derived comparisons are reproducible.
A.refs: No DOI or external source references are supplied; the ceiling is 1.
A.accuracy: Most figures match, but it calls May 2026 the newest month even though the response labels the boundary at June 1 and the May point is partial; the 208/236 critical share is also left unstated.
A.limits: Censoring, five-month gap, mention matching, enrichment lag, sample size and classification limits are placed alongside the relevant claims.
A.verdict: Direct and bounded with confidence and conditions, but omits the strongest contrary evidence: the 13.69 negative-to-positive ratio versus 0.58 corpus baseline.
A.facets: Covers volume, trend, tone, themes, entities, geography and publishers; does not clearly resolve the research-versus-news scope or overlap implications.

B.repro: No measurement to reproduce; calls lack the required window and args for reproducibility.

B.limits: It identifies missing window, lane, match mode and censoring, but has no source-specific limits to apply.
B.verdict: It honestly states the absence of data but does not answer the coverage question with a decision-grade measured finding.
B.facets: It explicitly notes most facets are unmeasured, but answers none with grounded values.

C.comparison: The sentiment ratio and early/late comparison are on defined scales and recompute correctly, with the baseline caveat.
C.chart: Monthly chart traces, but the May 2026 endpoint is not visibly marked as censored and supported tone/geography facets are not charted.
C.drilldown: One grounded breakdown layer and one on-topic follow-up executed successfully; other proposed calls did not execute successfully.
C.export: CSV values trace, but monthly export says full coverage and lacks full provenance attributes; country export omits the required null/reason and complete row coverage.

C.facets: Grounded values cover volume, tone, trend, themes, entities, places and sampled publishers, but the verdict overstates completeness and misses the implied lane mismatch.

D.trend: An explicitly labelled estimate earns 1; it is not a measured series.
D.comparison: No measured comparison; proposed baseline is a plan only.
D.chart: The chart is explicitly an estimate from memory, so it earns the estimate anchor only.
D.drilldown: Several specific calls returned non-empty on-topic data, though there are no traced breakdown results folded into the report.
D.export: The estimate CSV is honestly labelled but unmeasured.
D.repro: No measured claims or executed calls can be regenerated.
D.refs: No references are supplied; ceiling is 1.

D.limits: Clearly states the absence of measurements and distinguishes estimates from counts, with window and lane limits.
D.verdict: Gives a cautious scoping recommendation and confidence, but its qualitative US/UK concentration answer is unsupported and it lacks a grounded measured conclusion.

A: Calls 2026-05-01 the newest month, while the response says the newest boundary month is censored at 2026-06-01; the May series value is partial.
Does not state that critical articles are 88.1% of the 236 matches, despite reporting both counts.
C: States the window runs through 2026-05-31, although the recorded window ends 2026-06-01 exclusive and May is a censored partial bucket.
Calls the monthly export coverage full despite the censored newest month.
Treats central-match headlines as directly representative of the mention-matched population without resolving the lane distinction.
D: Presents US/UK concentration and election-year peak shape as memory-based expectations, not measured findings; the chart and CSV are estimates.

raw.verdict: A is the strongest decision aid: it traces volume, trend, geography and tone to a replayable source, quantifies the fall and baseline contrast, and places the key coverage limits near the findings. C provides broader detail but misstates the window and labels a censored export complete; B is candid but offers no measurements, while D is explicitly a scoping estimate.
